P3.title: Quantum Simulation via Stochastic Combination of Unitaries

P3.target: exponential with real/imaginary Pauli expansion; same finite P_m obtained by separating zeroth identity and collecting finite even/odd powers
P3.information_access: I1 Pauli coefficients and norms; Markov layering uses partial expansions, not generic I0 closure-free CTS
P3.decomposition: C+I+iS; real signed Pauli atoms plus identity/imaginary common-angle Euler group
P3.normalization: Lc+sqrt(1+Ls^2), Lc=sum_P abs(C_P), Ls=sum_P abs(S_P); Markov layers can increase norm vs full collection
P3.atom_class: signed Pauli or common-angle signed-Pauli rotation; Markov extension uses products of lower-block atoms
P3.classical_preprocessing: literal full word collection upper bound O(L^m); sparse dynamic programming or partial blocks can reduce it, so exhaustive expansion is not an intrinsic requirement
P3.sampling_semantics: positive coefficient/mu distribution; left and right samples independent for observable/channel use; exact finite block layering preserves first mean but not generally collected normalization
P3.audit_scope: C1-C5; no impossibility claim for future CTS extensions
